extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, care provider facilities, legal service providers, sponsors, and other stakeholders involved in care and placement of unaccompanied children
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory standards from ORR governing definitions, placement, care, restrictive placement criteria, assessments, notifications, and release procedures for unaccompanied children in ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOIR accredited representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a representative of a qualified nonprofit religious, charitable, social service, or other similar organization established in the United States and recognized by the Department of Justice in accordance with 8 CFR part 1292. An EOIR accredited representative who is representing a child in ORR custody may file a notice of such representation in order to receive updates on the unaccompanied child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family planning services
rubrics_metrics.description: Include, but are not limited to, FDA-approved contraceptive products (including emergency contraception), pregnancy testing and counseling, STI services, and referrals to appropriate specialists. The term does not include abortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abortion is treated separately under 'medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement' and is discussed in § 410.1307.

rubrics_metrics.name: Family Reunification Packet
rubrics_metrics.description: An application and supporting documentation which must be completed by a potential sponsor who wishes to have an unaccompanied child released from ORR to their care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR uses the application and supporting documentation, as well as other procedures, to determine the sponsor's ability to provide for the unaccompanied child's physical and mental well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heightened supervision facility
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility operated by a program, agency, or organization licensed by an appropriate State agency that meets standards for standard programs set forth in § 410.1302 and is designed for a child who requires close supervision but does not need placement in a secure facility, including an RTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides 24-hour supervision, custody, care, and treatment; maintains stricter security measures than a shelter (intensive staff supervision) to manage problem behavior and prevent running away; may have a secure perimeter but shall not have internal major restraining construction or procedures typical of juvenile detention or correctional facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home study
rubrics_metrics.description: An in-depth investigation of the potential sponsor's ability to ensure the child's safety and well-being, initiated by ORR as part of the sponsor suitability assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes investigation of living conditions, standard of care, and interviews with proposed sponsor and household members. Conducted when required by TVPRA, this part, and at ORR discretion (e.g., when safety is in question).

rubrics_metrics.name: Influx
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this part, a situation in which the net bed capacity of ORR's standard programs that is occupied or held for placement by unaccompanied children meets or exceeds 85 percent for a period of seven consecutive days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal guardian
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual who has been lawfully vested with the power and duty of caring for, including managing the property, rights, and affairs of, a child or incapacitated adult by a court of competent jurisdiction, foreign or domestic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal service provider
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization or individual attorney who provides legal services to unaccompanied children, either pro bono or through ORR funding for unaccompanied children's legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal service providers provide Know Your Rights presentations and screenings for legal relief to unaccompanied children, and/or direct legal representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBTQI+
rubrics_metrics.description: Means lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer or questioning, and intersex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Any device attached or adjacent to the child's body that the child cannot easily remove that restricts freedom of movement or normal access to the child's body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical services requiring heightened ORR involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes: (1) significant surgical or medical procedures; (2) abortions; and (3) medical services necessary to address threats to the life of or serious jeopardy to the health of an unaccompanied child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Concern (NOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument used by home study and post-release services providers, ORR care providers, and the ORR National Call Center staff to document and notify ORR of certain concerns that arise after a child is released from ORR care and custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Placement (NOP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written notice provided to unaccompanied children placed in restrictive placements explaining the reasons for placement and kept as part of the child's case file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The care provider facility must provide the NOP to the child within 48 hours after arrival at a restrictive placement and at minimum every 30 days while the child remains in a restrictive placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR
rubrics_metrics.description: Means the Office of Refugee Resettlement, Administration for Children and Families, U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR long-term home care
rubrics_metrics.description: An ORR-funded family or group home placement in a community-based setting used when ORR is unable to identify an appropriate sponsor during the pendency of legal proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Long-term home care" has the same meaning as "long-term foster care" as used in the definition of traditional foster care at 45 CFR 411.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR transitional home care
rubrics_metrics.description: An ORR-funded short-term placement in a family or group home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Transitional home care" has the same meaning as "transitional foster care" as used in the definition of traditional foster care at 45 CFR 411.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out of network placement (OON)
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility that provides physical care and services for individual unaccompanied children as requested by ORR on a case-by-case basis, operating under a single case agreement between ORR and the OON provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OON may include hospitals, restrictive settings, or other settings outside the ORR network of care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer restraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking or permitting other children to physically restrain another child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of physical force without the use of any device for the purpose of restraining a child's free movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Does not include briefly holding a child without undue force to calm or comfort them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering the unaccompanied child to the physical custody and care of either a care provider facility or an alternative to such a facility. A placed child is in the legal custody of ORR and may only be transferred or released by ORR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unaccompanied child remains in custody of a referring agency until physically transferred to a care provider facility or alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement Review Panel
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-member panel of ORR senior-level career staff with requisite child welfare experience convened to review requests for reconsideration of restrictive placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ORR staff member who was involved with the decision to step up a child to a restrictive placement may not serve as a Placement Review Panel member for that child's placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-release services (PRS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow-up services as used in the William Wilberforce TVPRA. ORR-approved services provided to a child and the child's sponsor after release, subject to available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance may include linking families to educational/community resources, home visits, case management, in-home counseling, and other social welfare services. When required by statute, the nature and extent are subject to available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level events
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations that affect the entire care provider facility and/or unaccompanied children and staff and require immediate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes death of staff/other adults/children in facility, major disturbances (shooting, riot, etc.), natural disasters (earthquake, flood, wildfire, etc.), and events affecting normal operations (long-term power outage, gas leaks, inoperable fire alarms, infectious disease outbreak).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prone physical restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: A restraint restricting a child's breathing, restricting or hyperextending a child's joints, or requiring a child to take an uncomfortable position.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRS provider
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization funded by ORR to connect the sponsor and unaccompanied child to community resources and other child welfare services following release from ORR custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychotropic medication(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Medication(s) prescribed for treatment of symptoms of psychosis or another mental, emotional, or behavioral disorder used to affect the central nervous system to influence behavior, cognition, or affective state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes categories: (1) psychomotor stimulants; (2) antidepressants; (3) antipsychotics/neuroleptics; (4) agents for control of mania or depression; (5) antianxiety agents; (6) sedatives, hypnotics, or other sleep-promoting medications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter
rubrics_metrics.description: For individuals with a disability: an interpreter (VRI or on-site) who can interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, including specialized vocabulary (e.g., sign language interpreters, oral transliterators). For limited English proficient individuals: an interpreter who has demonstrated proficiency in English and another language and can interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, preserving tone and adhering to interpreter ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For LEP: must interpret without changes, omissions, or additions and preserve tone, sentiment, emotional level; adhere to ethics including client confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified translator
rubrics_metrics.description: A translator who has demonstrated proficiency in writing/understanding both written English and at least one other written non-English language, can translate effectively, accurately, and impartially while preserving tone/sentiment, and adheres to translator ethics (including client confidentiality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Release (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discharge of an unaccompanied child to an ORR-vetted and approved sponsor. After release ORR does not have legal custody and the sponsor becomes responsible for the child's physical and mental well-being.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residential treatment center (RTC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sub-acute, time-limited, interdisciplinary, psycho-educational, therapeutic 24-hour structured program with community linkages provided through non-coercive, coordinated, individualized care, specialized services and interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RTCs provide highly customized care following community-based placement or more intensive intervention; are a type of secure facility and are not a standard program under this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictive placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Means a secure facility, including RTCs, or a heightened supervision facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runaway risk (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination that it is highly probable or reasonably certain that an unaccompanied child will attempt to abscond from ORR care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations must consider the totality of circumstances and should not be based solely on a past attempt to run away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The involuntary confinement of a child alone in a room or area from which the child is physically prevented from leaving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure facility
rubrics_metrics.description: A State or county juvenile detention facility or a secure ORR detention facility or a facility with separate accommodations for minors in a physically secure structure with staff able to control violent behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the most restrictive placement option for a child who poses a danger to self or others or has been charged with a criminal offense. A secure facility does not need to meet § 410.1302 and is not a standard program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shelter
rubrics_metrics.description: A kind of standard program in which all programmatic components are administered on-site, consistent with standards in § 410.1302.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-emergency situations that may immediately affect the safety and well-being of a child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes abuse or neglect in ORR care; sexual harassment/inappropriate sexual behavior; Staff Code of Conduct violations; contact/threats from trafficking/smuggling/organized crime; incidents involving law enforcement on site; potential fraud schemes against sponsors; pregnancy; separation from parent/legal guardian upon apprehension; mental health concerns; and use of safety measures such as restraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special needs unaccompanied child
rubrics_metrics.description: A child whose mental and/or physical condition requires special services and treatment by staff, due to alcohol/substance use, serious emotional disturbance, mental illness, intellectual/developmental disability, or a physical/chronic condition, or who has suffered serious neglect or abuse and requires services as a result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual (or entity) to whom ORR releases an unaccompanied child out of ORR custody in accordance with ORR's sponsor suitability assessment and release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of personnel requirements established by ORR to promote a safe environment for unaccompanied children, including protections from sexual abuse and sexual harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard program
rubrics_metrics.description: Any program, agency, or organization licensed by an appropriate State agency (or meets ORR-specified requirements where licensure is unavailable) to provide residential, group, transitional, or long-term home care services for dependent children, including family/group homes or facilities for special needs children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must meet standards in § 410.1302; all homes and facilities operated by a standard program shall be non-secure, though a facility for special needs children may maintain security permitted under State law or ORR requirements when necessary for protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tender age
rubrics_metrics.description: Means twelve years of age or younger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Movement of a child from one ORR care provider facility to another such that the receiving facility takes over physical custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR uses 'step up' and 'step down' to describe transfers to/from restrictive placements (e.g., shelter to heightened supervision = step up; heightened supervision to shelter = step down). Transfers between shelter and community-based care are neither step up nor step down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma bond
rubrics_metrics.description: When a trafficker uses rewards and punishments within cycles of abuse to foster a powerful emotional connection with the victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trauma-informed
rubrics_metrics.description: A system/standard/process/practice that realizes the widespread impact of trauma, understands paths for recovery, recognizes signs and symptoms of trauma in children, families, staff, and others, and responds by integrating knowledge about trauma into policies, procedures, and practices while actively resisting re-traumatization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unaccompanied child/children (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A child who: (1) has no lawful immigration status in the U.S.; (2) has not attained 18 years of age; and (3) for whom there is no parent or legal guardian in the U.S. or no parent/legal guardian available to provide care and physical custody.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unaccompanied Refugee Minors (URM) Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The child welfare services program available pursuant to 8 U.S.C. 1522(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for care and placement (§ 410.1003)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR principles: treat children with dignity, respect, and special concern for vulnerability; hold children in safe and sanitary facilities consistent with their vulnerability; plan and provide care based on individual needs and strengths; encourage developmentally appropriate participation in decision-making; strive to provide quality care tailored to individual needs and protect children from traffickers and victimization; place children in least restrictive settings in their best interests considering danger to self/others and runaway risk; consult parents/legal guardians/advocates/attorneys as needed when requesting information or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles apply within all placements and guide placement determinations and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORR custody and emergency physical transfer (§ 410.1004)
rubrics_metrics.description: All unaccompanied children placed by ORR in care provider facilities remain in legal custody of ORR and may be transferred or released only with ORR approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In an emergency, a care provider facility may transfer temporary physical custody prior to securing ORR approval but must notify ORR as soon as practicable and in all cases within 8 hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and placement timeline (§ 410.1101)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR accepts referrals from any Federal department/agency at any time; upon notification that a child is unaccompanied and must be transferred to ORR custody ORR identifies an appropriate placement and notifies the referring agency within 24 hours whenever possible and no later than 48 hours, barring exceptional circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR works with referring agency consistent with 8 U.S.C. 1232(b)(3). Exceptional circumstances may include court decrees, influx, emergencies, medical emergencies (epidemic/pandemic), remote apprehension, child posing danger or criminal charges needing more info, or unforeseeable acts preventing timely placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider facility types and OON placements (§ 410.1102)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place children in shelters, group homes, individual family homes, heightened supervision facilities, secure facilities (including RTCs), and may place children in OON placements under certain limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In periods of influx or emergency ORR may place children in facilities that may not meet standard program standards but meet standards in subpart I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement considerations (§ 410.1103)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall place each child in the least restrictive setting in the child's best interest and appropriate to age and individualized needs, consistent with ensuring timely appearance before DHS/immigration courts and protecting the child and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant factors include danger to self; danger to others/community; runaway risk; trafficking or other safety concerns; age; gender; LGBTQI+ status; disability; any specialized services/treatment required; criminal background; location of potential sponsor and safe release options; behavior; siblings in ORR custody; language access; pregnancy/parenting status; location of apprehension; length of stay. ORR may use referring agency info, assessment tools, interviews, and records from local/state/federal agencies. ORR must review restrictive placements at least every 30 days. Care provider facilities must accept placements unless specific reasons (lack of bed space; conflict with licensing; missing medical clearance for significant illness; inability to meet disability-related needs without fundamental alteration). Denials require written requests to ORR with individualized reasons and ORR approval; ORR may follow up to find solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default placement in standard program (§ 410.1104)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR places all unaccompanied children in standard programs that are not restrictive, except where the child meets criteria for restrictive placement in § 410.1105 or in the event of an emergency or influx requiring expedited placement under subpart I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for secure facility placement (§ 410.1105(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place a child in a secure facility (not an RTC) only if: (i) the child has been charged with or convicted of a crime or is subject of delinquency proceedings and ORR deems those circumstances show the child poses a danger to self or others (excluding isolated non-violent offenses and petty offenses); (ii) while in DHS/ORR custody or presence of immigration officer/ORR official/contracted staff, the child committed or made credible threats to commit violent/malicious acts; or (iii) child engaged in conduct while in a restrictive placement that has been unacceptably disruptive of facility functioning and removal is necessary to ensure welfare of the child or others (e.g., substance use, stealing, fighting, intimidation, sexually predatory behavior), and ORR determines the child poses a danger to self or others based on such conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will not place a child in a secure facility if less restrictive alternatives in the child's best interests are available and appropriate; alternatives include heightened supervision or other non-secure care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for heightened supervision facility placement (§ 410.1105(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place a child in a heightened supervision facility if the child: (i) has been unacceptably disruptive to normal shelter functioning such that transfer is necessary to ensure welfare; (ii) is a runaway risk; (iii) has displayed a pattern or severity of behavior prior to or while in ORR care requiring increased supervision; (iv) has a non-violent criminal/delinquent history not warranting secure facility; or (v) is assessed as ready for step-down from a secure facility, including an RTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for RTC placement (§ 410.1105(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A child with serious mental health or behavioral health issues may be placed into an RTC only if evaluated and determined to be a danger to self or others by a licensed psychologist or psychiatrist consulted by ORR or a care provider facility, including a determination by clear and convincing evidence documented in the child's case file or referral documentation that an RTC is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR may place a child at an OON RTC when a licensed clinician determines needs cannot be met within ORR's RTC network or an OON RTC would best meet identified needs. Criteria for RTC placements also apply to OON RTCs. Care provider facilities may request transfers to an RTC per § 410.1601(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment for particular services and treatment (§ 410.1106)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall assess each child to determine whether the child requires particular services and treatment (e.g., for disability, substance use, history of neglect/abuse, tender age, pregnancy/parenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If individualized needs require particular services/equipment, ORR shall place the child, whenever possible, in a licensed program where children with disabilities can interact with people without disabilities to the fullest extent, and shall make reasonable modifications so children with disabilities have equal access in the most integrated setting appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runaway risk determination factors (§ 410.1107)
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining runaway risk ORR considers whether: (a) the child is under a final order of removal; (b) immigration history includes prior breach of bond, failure to appear, indebtedness to smugglers, or previous removal; (c) child previously absconded or attempted to abscond from custody; (d) child displayed behaviors indicative of flight or expressed intent to run away; (e) evidence child is indebted to, experiencing trauma bond to, or threatened by a trafficker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and services for children of unaccompanied children (§ 410.1108)
rubrics_metrics.description: If unaccompanied children and their children are referred together, ORR shall place them in the same facility except in unusual or emergency situations (hospitalization, child's request, allegations of abuse/neglect warranting temporary separation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR provides the same care and services to the children of unaccompanied children as to unaccompanied children, as appropriate, regardless of immigration/citizenship status. U.S. citizen children are eligible for public benefits/services to the same extent as other U.S. citizens; care provider facilities shall submit applications for benefits on their behalf and exhaust such benefits before using ORR-funded services to the greatest extent practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice of legal rights (§ 410.1109)
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall promptly provide each child in its custody, in a language and manner the child understands, with: (1) a State-by-State list of free legal service providers compiled and annually updated by ORR as part of a Legal Resource Guide; (2) an explanation of the right of potential review including statement about least restrictive settings and right to consult a lawyer; and (3) a presentation regarding their legal rights as provided under § 410.1309(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR shall not engage in retaliatory actions against legal service providers or any representative because of advocacy or appearance in an action adverse to ORR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of release subpart (§ 410.1200)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers policies and procedures used to release, without unnecessary delay, an unaccompanied child from ORR custody to a vetted and approved sponsor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsors to whom ORR releases a child (§ 410.1201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to sponsor suitability assessment, ORR shall release a minor without unnecessary delay when detention is not required, in the following order of preference: (1) a parent; (2) a legal guardian; (3) an adult relative; (4) an adult individual or entity designated by the parent or guardian (by declaration under penalty of perjury or other satisfactory document); (5) a standard program willing to accept legal custody; (6) an adult individual or entity seeking custody in ORR discretion when no other likely alternative to long-term custody exists and family reunification is not reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release is subject to assessment of sponsor suitability and ORR's release procedures.
